samples.identification: Loopback WebDAV NTLM capture proof of concept
evidence: Main starts an HttpListener on localhost:8080 before invoking cmd /c net use against the same loopback WebDAV port.
The request loop appends Authorization headers verbatim to a local file and returns HTTP 401 with a fixed NTLMSSP type-2 challenge.
The Base64 challenge decodes to a 48-byte NTLMSSP message with message type 2. No successful handshake, relay, elevation, or external exfiltration is asserted.
samples.criticality: Two suspicious profiles: coercion and authorization recording are dual-use techniques, even though this program deliberately captures authentication material.

samples.identification: Concealed browser task execution and result callback
evidence: Decoded inline JavaScript fetches a remote response as a Blob, assigns an object URL to an anchor, sets a .000 download filename, and clicks the anchor.
Batch starts Edge at 10000,10000 with a 1x1 window and disabled certificate checks, waits, and copies downloaded .000 files into a temporary .cmd path.
cmd /c executes that same copied path; stdout and stderr are redirected to a temporary result file. curl uploads that same result path to the fetch endpoint; DEL removes the staged script and result.
No recurring polling or actor attribution is inferred.
fixes: Require Blob download preparation in the concealed staging composite.
Classify generic curl invocation/URLs independently of transfer direction.
Do not mistake 2>&1 for command chaining.

samples.unpacking: UPX 5.2.1 successfully unpacked a copy; original bytes preserved. Build metadata reports salat-stealer, Go 1.26.0, windows/amd64, CGO_ENABLED=0.
evidence: main.main at 0x1402c0840 invokes elevation or Defender exclusions, static installation, system information collection, and runSession in a goroutine.
connectTCP at 0x1402c26c0 loads configured host 217.60.6.239 and port 7777 and calls crypto/tls.dial. This endpoint was not contacted.

runSession -> recvLoop -> recvPkt -> recvLoop.gowrap1 -> dispatch. Dispatch passes the received command field to execCommand at 0x1402c4ea0, which invokes hidden cmd /c and CombinedOutput; dispatch returns results through session.send.

dispatch.func1 at 0x1402c43c0 calls Steal, Base64-encodes its ZIP result, and calls session.send. Steal -> stealBrowsers reaches wallet/Telegram collection, Chromium/Gecko extraction code, and screenshot archive creation.
stealWallets at 0x1402c9b40 builds wallet-root paths, walks them, and calls stealWallets.func1 -> os.ReadFile -> addToZip.
elevateFodhelper at 0x1402c14c0 writes the current executable into the HKCU ms-settings open-command association, sets an empty DelegateExecute, runs fodhelper.exe, and removes the hijack key.
addDefenderExclusion at 0x1402c0be0 constructs hidden PowerShell Add-MpPreference commands for executable and directory exclusions.
staticinstall at 0x1402befe0 copies itself, configures Run keys or a scheduled task, applies hidden/system attributes, and relaunches the installed copy.
handshake at 0x1402c20e0 receives an RSA public key, generates a random AES key, wraps it using RSA OAEP, and establishes AES-GCM framing. OAEP is not evidence of ransomware.

tcpStreamMic and tcpStreamCam construct FFmpeg DirectShow capture subprocesses, read stdout, and send the resulting data through session.send. These are attempted capabilities requiring a working FFmpeg and valid capture device.
limitations: tcpStreamScreen at 0x1402c46a0 only sleeps and checks a stop flag; it performs no capture or network send. Removed its capability trait and excluded it from the sensor profile.
SQLiteDriver.Open at 0x14014f9a0 returns nil and the no-CGO stub error. Chromium/Gecko SQLite extraction code is present, but database extraction cannot succeed with this linked driver.
External sandbox and VirusTotal pages were inaccessible during review; the verdict rests on local execution-path evidence.

FFmpeg selectors are the literal placeholders audio=... and video=...; successful microphone/camera recording is not established. The code nevertheless attempts capture, reads subprocess stdout, and sends it.
